subject: plot each layer in its own color

messages.author: 6d3f7222550fe21b
messages.subject: plot each layer in its own color
parts:
Below are two different syntaxes that explicitly define three layers, each with its own color, and then plot them on top of each other.

But both syntaxes also create a distracting, silly legend.

(1) How can I suppress the legend? But, more important ...

(2) Legend suppression is a workaround. The creation of the legend in the first place suggests that I have not approached the problem correctly. Is there a way to make this plot that does *not* require a workaround?

(3) If there is to be a legend at all, it should say something like "data", "interpolation", "least squares line" and should show in turn a red dot (no line through it), a green line (without dot), and a blue line (without dot). How would one elegantly do that in ggplot2?

# One syntax:

set.seed(7)

DUT<-data.frame(eks=rnorm(9))

DUT$why<-DUT$eks * 0.3 + rnorm(9)/5

pointlayer<-layer(data=DUT, mapping=aes(x=eks, y=why, color="red"), geom="point", geom_params=list(shape=1))

linelayer<-layer(data=DUT, mapping=aes(x=eks, y=why, color="blue"), geom="line")

smoothlayer<- layer(data=DUT, mapping=aes(x=eks, y=why, color="green"), geom="smooth", method="lm", se=FALSE)

ggplot() + pointlayer + linelayer + smoothlayer

# Another syntax:

DUT$pointcolor<- "red"

DUT$linecolor<-"blue"

DUT$smoothcolor<-"green"

pointlayer2<-layer(data=DUT, mapping=aes(x=eks, y=why, color=pointcolor), geom="point", geom_params=list(shape=1))

linelayer2<-layer(data=DUT, mapping=aes(x=eks, y=why, color=linecolor), geom="line")

smoothlayer2<- layer(data=DUT, mapping=aes(x=eks, y=why, color=smoothcolor), geom="smooth", method="lm", se=FALSE)

ggplot() + pointlayer2 + linelayer2 + smoothlayer2

Thanks

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: plot each layer in its own color
parts:
If you want to keep using the verbose layer syntax, use

pointlayer<-layer(data=DUT, mapping=aes(x=eks, y=why), color="pink",
geom="point", geom_params=list(shape=1, color="red"))

linelayer<-layer(data=DUT, mapping=aes(x=eks, y=why), geom="line",
geom_parames=list(color="blue"))

smoothlayer<- layer(data=DUT, mapping=aes(x=eks, y=why),
geom="smooth", geom_params=list(color="green"),
stat_params=list(method="lm", se=FALSE))

The main thing you seem to have been tripped up on is the difference
between setting an aesthetic to a fixed value versus mapping it to a
variable. To do the former, set it outside the aes() call (or inside
geom_parames or stat_parames lists as in my example above). To do the
latter, set it inside the aes() call (this will generate a legend
unless you turn it off).

Best,
Ista

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: plot each layer in its own color
parts:
Hi:

This appears to get you 99% of the way there, I believe, including the legend:

# The 'shortcut way':
ggplot(data = DUT, aes(x = eks, y = why)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = 'Data'), shape = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = 'Interpolation')) +
  geom_smooth(aes(colour = 'Least squares line'), method = 'lm', se = FALSE) +
  labs(x = 'x', y = 'y', colour = 'Type') +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c('Data' = 'red', 'Interpolation' = 'blue',
                             'Least squares line' = 'green'))

# The layered way:
pointlayer<-layer(data=DUT, mapping=aes(x=eks, y=why, color = 'Data'),
                  geom="point", geom_params=list(shape=1))

linelayer<-layer(data=DUT, mapping=aes(x=eks, y=why, color = 'Interpolation'),
                 geom="line")

smoothlayer<- layer(data=DUT, mapping=aes(x=eks, y=why, color = 'Least squares line'),
                    geom="smooth", stat_params=list(method="lm", se=FALSE))

ggplot() + pointlayer + linelayer + smoothlayer +
  labs(x = 'x', y = 'y') +
  scale_color_manual(name = 'Type',
                     values = c('Data' = 'red', 'Interpolation' = 'blue',
                                'Least squares line' = 'green'))

You'll need a hack to pick and choose among geom types in the legend. The problem is that you use color for both points and lines, so what gets rendered in the legend is (go figure) points and lines. See p. 111 of Hadley's text. In base graphics, there is both an lty and pch argument to legend() - if you want one but not the other, one can be set to NULL in the appropriate location of the vector. There is no such analogue in ggplot2 AFAIK. Hadley could tell you if something is in the works on the development side, or perhaps someone can hack the legend code to add such a feature and post it here. Absent that, the legend glyphs are what they are, and the legend code is behaving as documented.

HTH,
Dennis
